name: Phanuel
overview: Phanuel is a male member of the tribe of Asher, known primarily as the father of Anna the prophetess. His mention in Scripture is brief but significant due to his connection to Anna, a devoted servant of God. No additional personal notes or details about his life are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Phanuel means 'face of God [El],' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names. This proper name highlights a connection to God but was not given directly by God. The meaning underscores a reverent association with God's presence.
familyAndRelationships: Phanuel is identified explicitly as a descendant of the tribe of Asher and is noted as the father of Anna, the prophetess. Scripture does not provide further details about his family beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Phanuel's significance lies chiefly in his role as the father of Anna, who is recognized as a prophetess. Through this relationship, he is connected to the prophetic witness in the New Testament, underscoring the faithfulness of his lineage within the tribe of Asher. His mention in Luke 2:36 situates him within the biblical narrative that highlights God's ongoing work through faithful individuals and families.
